## Classes

### <a name="heplify"></a>`heplify`

heplify captures VoIP signalling (SIP, and optionally RTCP, RTP, DNS, LOG
or Diameter) and forwards it as HEP to a HOMER heplify-server. Every
parameter has a default in the module's Hiera data, so the usual way to
configure the agent is with `heplify::*` keys in your own Hiera.

The defaults capture SIP on ports 5060-5090 on every interface and send
HEPv3 over UDP to a heplify-server on the same host (127.0.0.1:9060).

#### Examples

##### Capture SIP and send it to a heplify-server on the same host

```puppet
include heplify
```

##### Send to a remote heplify-server over TCP from a single interface

```puppet
class { 'heplify':
  interface     => 'eth0',
  hep_host      => 'homer.example.com',
  hep_port      => 9061,
  hep_transport => 'tcp',
}
```

##### <a name="-heplify--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `String[1]`

heplify release to install, for example `'2.0.28'`. With
`install_method => 'package'` this is the package version.

##### <a name="-heplify--install_method"></a>`install_method`

Data type: `Enum['binary', 'package', 'none']`

`binary` downloads the release binary, `package` installs `package_name`
from a repository you manage, `none` leaves installation to you.

##### <a name="-heplify--download_base_url"></a>`download_base_url`

Data type: `String[1]`

Base URL for release binaries. The file fetched is
`<download_base_url>/<version>/heplify_linux_<amd64|arm64>`. Point it at
an internal mirror if nodes cannot reach GitHub.

##### <a name="-heplify--checksums"></a>`checksums`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Hash[Enum['amd64', 'arm64'], Heplify::Sha256]]`

SHA-256 checksums of release binaries, keyed by version and then by
architecture (`amd64`, `arm64`). Merged across your Hiera hierarchy, so
adding a new version does not drop the ones shipped with the module.

##### <a name="-heplify--checksum"></a>`checksum`

Data type: `Optional[Heplify::Sha256]`

SHA-256 checksum of the binary. Overrides the `checksums` entry for this
node. When neither is set the download is not verified.

##### <a name="-heplify--package_name"></a>`package_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Package to install when `install_method` is `package`.

##### <a name="-heplify--install_dir"></a>`install_dir`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Directory holding the versioned binaries (`heplify-<version>`).

##### <a name="-heplify--bin_path"></a>`bin_path`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Path the service runs; a symlink to the current versioned binary when
`install_method` is `binary`.

##### <a name="-heplify--config_dir"></a>`config_dir`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Directory for `heplify.json`.

##### <a name="-heplify--interface"></a>`interface`

Data type: `String[1]`

Capture device, for example `any` or `eth0`.

##### <a name="-heplify--socket_type"></a>`socket_type`

Data type: `Enum['afpacket', 'pcap']`

Capture method: `afpacket` or `pcap`.

##### <a name="-heplify--promisc"></a>`promisc`

Data type: `Boolean`

Put the interface into promiscuous mode.

##### <a name="-heplify--capture_mode"></a>`capture_mode`

Data type: `Array[Heplify::CaptureMode, 1]`

Protocols to capture. Each one widens the kernel capture filter, so
list only what you need.

##### <a name="-heplify--sip_port_min"></a>`sip_port_min`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

Lowest SIP port to capture.

##### <a name="-heplify--sip_port_max"></a>`sip_port_max`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

Highest SIP port to capture.

##### <a name="-heplify--tcp_reassembly"></a>`tcp_reassembly`

Data type: `Boolean`

Reassemble TCP streams, needed for SIP over TCP.

##### <a name="-heplify--sip_reassembly"></a>`sip_reassembly`

Data type: `Boolean`

Reassemble SIP messages split across TCP segments.

##### <a name="-heplify--ip_defrag"></a>`ip_defrag`

Data type: `Boolean`

Reassemble fragmented IP packets.

##### <a name="-heplify--vlan"></a>`vlan`

Data type: `Boolean`

Capture VLAN-tagged traffic.

##### <a name="-heplify--bpf_filter"></a>`bpf_filter`

Data type: `String`

Custom BPF filter. Empty means heplify builds one from the capture
protocols and ports.

##### <a name="-heplify--hep_host"></a>`hep_host`

Data type: `Stdlib::Host`

Address of the heplify-server.

##### <a name="-heplify--hep_port"></a>`hep_port`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

HEP port on the heplify-server.

##### <a name="-heplify--hep_transport"></a>`hep_transport`

Data type: `Enum['udp', 'tcp', 'tls']`

Transport to the heplify-server: `udp`, `tcp` or `tls`.

##### <a name="-heplify--hep_password"></a>`hep_password`

Data type: `Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]`

HEP node password, if the heplify-server requires one. The config file
diff is hidden from reports when this is set.

##### <a name="-heplify--node_name"></a>`node_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

HEP node name reported to HOMER.

##### <a name="-heplify--node_id"></a>`node_id`

Data type: `Integer[0]`

HEP node ID reported to HOMER.

##### <a name="-heplify--deduplicate"></a>`deduplicate`

Data type: `Boolean`

Drop duplicate packets, for example when `interface` is `any` and
traffic crosses a bridge. Also hides genuine retransmissions.

##### <a name="-heplify--discard_methods"></a>`discard_methods`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

SIP methods to drop before sending, for example `['OPTIONS']`.

##### <a name="-heplify--log_level"></a>`log_level`

Data type: `Enum['debug', 'info', 'warn', 'error']`

heplify log level.

##### <a name="-heplify--config_overrides"></a>`config_overrides`

Data type: `Hash`

Hash deep-merged over the generated `heplify.json`, for any heplify
setting without a dedicated parameter. Arrays are replaced, not merged.

##### <a name="-heplify--manage_service"></a>`manage_service`

Data type: `Boolean`

Manage the systemd unit and service.

##### <a name="-heplify--service_name"></a>`service_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Name of the systemd service.

##### <a name="-heplify--service_ensure"></a>`service_ensure`

Data type: `Stdlib::Ensure::Service`

Whether the service should be running or stopped.

##### <a name="-heplify--service_enable"></a>`service_enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the service starts at boot.

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

systemd units heplify is ordered after, in addition to

### <a name="heplify--server"></a>`heplify::server`

heplify-server receives HEP from capture agents (such as the `heplify`
class in this module) and from SIP servers that send HEP natively, and
stores it in a database for the HOMER web UI. Every parameter has a
default in the module's Hiera data.

The defaults listen for HEP on UDP 0.0.0.0:9060 and store HOMER 7 data in
a local PostgreSQL as `homer_user` with the password `homer_password`, the
credentials homer-app uses by default. The module does not manage the
database: create the `homer_data` and `homer_config` databases and the
user beforehand (see the README).

#### Examples

##### Collector with a local PostgreSQL and homer-app's default credentials

```puppet
include heplify::server
```

##### Collector with your own database password

```puppet
class { 'heplify::server':
  db_password => Sensitive('change-me'),
}
```

##### Change individual heplify-server settings from Hiera

```puppet
heplify::server::db_password: 'change-me'
heplify::server::settings:
  DBAddr: 'db.example.com:5432'
  PromAddr: '127.0.0.1:9096'
```

##### <a name="-heplify--server--version"></a>`version`

Data type: `String[1]`

heplify-server release to install, for example `'1.60.1'`. With
`install_method => 'package'` this is the package version.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--install_method"></a>`install_method`

Data type: `Enum['binary', 'package', 'none']`

`binary` downloads the release binary, `package` installs `package_name`
from a repository you manage, `none` leaves installation to you.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--download_base_url"></a>`download_base_url`

Data type: `String[1]`

Base URL for release binaries. The file fetched is
`<download_base_url>/v<version>/heplify-server` on amd64 and
`<download_base_url>/v<version>/heplify-server-arm64` on arm64.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--checksums"></a>`checksums`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Hash[Enum['amd64', 'arm64'], Heplify::Sha256]]`

SHA-256 checksums of release binaries, keyed by version and then by
architecture (`amd64`, `arm64`). Merged across your Hiera hierarchy.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--checksum"></a>`checksum`

Data type: `Optional[Heplify::Sha256]`

SHA-256 checksum of the binary. Overrides the `checksums` entry for this
node. When neither is set the download is not verified.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--package_name"></a>`package_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Package to install when `install_method` is `package`.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--install_dir"></a>`install_dir`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Directory holding the versioned binaries (`heplify-server-<version>`).

##### <a name="-heplify--server--bin_path"></a>`bin_path`

Data type: `Stdlib::Absolutepath`

Path the service runs; a symlink to the current versioned binary when
`install_method` is `binary`.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--config_file"></a>`config_file`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/.*\.toml\z/]`

Path of the generated configuration. heplify-server only reads files
whose name contains `.toml`.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--manage_user"></a>`manage_user`

Data type: `Boolean`

Create the system user and group the service runs as.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--user"></a>`user`

Data type: `String[1]`

User the service runs as.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--group"></a>`group`

Data type: `String[1]`

Group the service runs as; it can read the configuration file.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--settings"></a>`settings`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Heplify::ServerSetting]`

heplify-server settings written to `config_file`, keyed by their
heplify-server names (`HEPAddr`, `DBAddr`, `PromAddr`, ...). Deep-merged
across your Hiera hierarchy over the module defaults. Settings you leave
out take heplify-server's built-in defaults.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--db_password"></a>`db_password`

Data type: `Variant[String, Sensitive[String]]`

Database password, written as `DBPass`. Converted to `Sensitive` on
lookup. When any password in the configuration is set, the file diff
is left out of reports.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--allow_db_superuser"></a>`allow_db_superuser`

Data type: `Boolean`

heplify-server treats the database users `postgres`, `root` and `admin`
as administrators: it creates `homer_user` itself and, on PostgreSQL,
grants it the `postgres` role, making it a database superuser. Catalog
compilation fails for those users unless this is `true`.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--manage_service"></a>`manage_service`

Data type: `Boolean`

Manage the systemd unit and service.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--service_name"></a>`service_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

Name of the systemd service.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--service_ensure"></a>`service_ensure`

Data type: `Stdlib::Ensure::Service`

Whether the service should be running or stopped.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--service_enable"></a>`service_enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the service starts at boot.

##### <a name="-heplify--server--after_units"></a>`after_units`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

systemd units heplify-server is ordered after, in addition to
`network-online.target`. Units that do not exist are ignored by systemd.
